t: Reproducible Build Verifier - public implementations survey
title: Reproducible Build Verifier - public implementations survey
definition: Checks whether the same inputs produce equivalent build outputs.
description:
Reproducible Build Verifier is one of the fundamental capabilities an AI needs to build things on demand: Checks whether the same inputs produce equivalent build outputs. In the real world this capability is delivered by a rich ecosystem of tools, libraries and platforms. This database is the public edition - a fact-checked survey of the real implementations, the real techniques they share, the standards they follow, and laddered drills that teach the capability hands-on.

No single tool owns Reproducible Build Verifier. Competing implementations emphasize different trade-offs: speed against flexibility, simplicity against power, integration against independence. The implementation spotlights in this database document the notable real ones - what each does, where it excels, and how it serves Reproducible Build Verifier. Together they map the territory as it actually exists.

Every record carries a runnable demonstration program, because tools are understood by use. Run the demos with node, compare the implementations, practice the drills, and the Reproducible Build Verifier capability becomes something you can reach for - with full knowledge of which real tool fits which job.

t: Mercurial - related Reproducible Build Verifier technology
title: Mercurial - related Reproducible Build Verifier technology
definition: Clean distributed VCS alternative.
description:
Mercurial is not itself a Reproducible Build Verifier, but it belongs in this survey because real Reproducible Build Verifier work leans on it. Clean distributed VCS alternative.

In a Reproducible Build Verifier build it shows up when the team already lives in its ecosystem. The design favors boring reliability over cleverness: well-trodden paths, clear errors, and behavior you can reason about without reading the source. Knowing the surrounding technology is part of knowing the capability - the best Reproducible Build Verifier practitioners can say exactly where their tool ends and its neighbors begin.

For builders, Mercurial is the pragmatic pick for most builds as supporting technology. The demo program exercises a core idea from its domain - run it with node and watch each step.

title: Reproducible Build Verifier definition of done - practitioner discipline
definition: The definition of done discipline for Reproducible Build Verifier: checks whether the same inputs produce equivalent build outputs..
description:
definition of done is the Reproducible Build Verifier discipline: Checks whether the same inputs produce equivalent build outputs. It turns Reproducible Build Verifier from an event into a repeatable capability.

In practice this means: log every decision with its reason, so the next builder inherits understanding; verify outputs against the original request, not against your hopes; keep a failure log: what broke, why, and what now prevents it Teams that follow the discipline get predictable builds; teams that skip it get interesting stories. t: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reproducible Buil
title: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reproducible Buil
definition: Ladder drill (foundation): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reproducible Build Verifier from a one-paragraph brief.
description:
Drill (FOUNDATION): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reproducible Build Verifier from a one-paragraph brief

Read the brief twice. List every input the Reproducible Build Verifier needs, every output it must produce, and one contract each input-output pair must satisfy. Work it by hand first, then run the demo program and compare its trace against your own reasoning. When they agree, the concept is yours.

Success criterion: you can list them from memory without looking at the brief
